note: Campaign money as filed: FEC itemized receipts and disbursements for federal candidates, and Georgia Campaign Contribution Disclosure Reports the crawler read or that were imported. Each gift is the filer's own line (u is the filing it was read from); donors are matched across filings by name and address, which can split one person or merge two with the same name. Only a candidate's own campaign committees count as what the candidate raised; a leadership PAC the candidate runs is listed as its own committee (pac_of), and a joint fundraising committee's money is counted where it was transferred. Each federal campaign carries fec: the FEC's own receipts total for its committees, against which the itemized lines are checked. A platform's lump line (WinRed, ActBlue) is counted in what the recipient raised and listed under conduits, but the platform is not ranked as a donor; a gift earmarked through a conduit (a platform or a PAC such as AIPAC PAC) is the person's own, listed under via with the conduit named. Memo lines, the same line read twice, and transfers between a candidate's own committees are left out. Filings carry no demographic data beyond employer, occupation and address. review marks rows parsed from a scanned PDF. Each recipient's and gift's money is also split by two-year election cycle (cy; 2025 and 2026 are the 2026 cycle, as the FEC counts them), with the first and last date of the lines in it, and by calendar year (yr, the same shape). self is the candidate's own money (gifts filed under the candidate's own name, or filed as Self). A donor's kind (person, org, committee) is the source type the Georgia filing itself gives, and the name only where the filing gives none. A gift marked self_inferred is counted as the candidate's own money because a person of the campaign's surname gave it more than $100,000, which Georgia law (O.C.G.A. 21-5-41) lets no one but the candidate give. kinds is each recipient's money from named donors by kind; totals covers every line. A committee whose name does not carry its candidate's full name is linked to the candidate only by config/committee_links.yaml, each link with its source (links: committee and source; link_src: the first); committees lists the committees counted under a candidate. held is the number of the campaign's FEC lines waiting to be read again: its federal total is incomplete until then. fec_cy is the FEC's own totals for a federal campaign's committees per cycle (receipts, gifts under $200 included; through: the newest report's end date): the page shows these as the campaign's money, the itemized lines as the detail. moved is money another committee of the same candidate moved to this one (a leadership committee paying into the campaign, an old campaign account into the new one: total, from whom, by cycle and year): it was counted where it was first given, so it is not in raised here.
hold: Federal campaign money (FEC) is being read again with the FEC's own line codes: a check found FEC memo lines counted as gifts (one AIPAC PAC figure was counted 20 times). Federal candidates come back as each campaign is read again; until then their money is left out rather than shown wrong. The itemized gifts of 1 federal campaign (Jon Ossoff) are still being read from the FEC, newest first: their listed donors cover only what has been read so far, while their totals are the FEC's own.
